projects.title: Legal Discovery Intelligence Graph
projects.summary: A deployed Graph RAG investigation workspace with cited evidence, entity graphs, and reproducible evaluation.
projects.outcome: A public synthetic-matter investigation workflow combines vector and graph retrieval, cited evidence, timelines, privilege/PII flags, calibrated refusal, and an auditable case brief.

deployment.runtime: Flask + gunicorn with an ONNX embedding backend

disclosure.source: Repository-generated Project Falcon synthetic legal-discovery corpus, seed 42
disclosure.license: Repository project license; no third-party client or matter data
disclosure.permittedUse: Portfolio demonstration, deterministic evaluation, and engineering research
includedFields: Fictional documents, entities, events, amounts, relationships, and planted evidence
Synthetic privilege and PII-like labels used solely for evaluation
excludedFields: Real client, employee, custodian, matter, communication, and personal data
Production legal advice, privilege determinations, and discovery decisions
deployedArtifactContents: Synthetic corpus-derived indexes and graph records
Read-only Flask application and committed aggregate evaluation artifacts
No real discovery files or client data

evidence.claim: Entity-mention extraction achieved micro F1 0.887 strict on the committed synthetic corpus.
evidence.method: One-to-one strict span matching against generator-emitted gold labels
evidence.scope: 2,223 entity mentions in a deterministic 455-document synthetic corpus, seed 42
evidence.caveat: Clean templated text materially overstates expected performance on real discovery documents.

evidence.claim: Hybrid retrieval achieved R@10 0.857 and graph expansion improved relationship hit@5 to 0.833.
evidence.method: Versioned labeled-query evaluation comparing vector-only and graph-expanded retrieval
evidence.scope: 38 categorized retrieval queries over the 455-document synthetic corpus
evidence.environment: Local integration evaluation against configured vector and graph stores
evidence.caveat: Graph expansion improves relationship queries but can dilute dense-corpus ranking at larger k.

evidence.claim: Privilege and synthetic-PII rules achieved F1 1.0 on clean templated text.
evidence.method: Document-level rule evaluation against synthetic gold labels

evidence.claim: The current Render application root returned HTTP 200.
evidence.method: Read-only HTTP request with redirects followed; no user data submitted
evidence.caveat: HTTP reachability is not availability, confidentiality, security, or production-readiness evidence.

evidence.claim: The corpus, gold labels, people, organizations, identifiers, and events are generated and fictional.
evidence.method: Versioned generator and data/evaluation documentation review

narrative.recruiterSummary: Legal discovery teams need to connect people, events, documents, and evidence without losing the source trail. This project demonstrates that workflow on a fully fictional matter: reviewers can search, traverse relationships, inspect a timeline, and open cited documents while the product clearly distinguishes evidence from generated structure.
narrative.technicalNarrative: A deterministic generator emits a 455-document corpus and gold labels. Offline pipelines extract entities/events, create pgvector embeddings, and load Neo4j relationships. The deployed Flask app uses an ONNX embedding backend within Render's memory limit, fuses vector and graph retrieval, applies a calibrated refusal threshold, and renders cited results, graphs, timelines, flags, and evaluation artifacts.
limitations: Synthetic templated text is materially cleaner than real discovery data.
The public demo has no real-client security or matter-isolation posture.
Free-tier services can sleep or pause and do not establish an availability SLO.
Privilege/PII flags are research aids, not legal or privacy determinations.
scalabilityRoadmap: Add authenticated matter isolation, role-based access, audit retention, and encrypted document storage
Introduce OCR and robust parsing for scans, forwarded chains, and production document variance
Move ingestion and indexing to background workers with versioned index promotion
Add real-world benchmark sets under appropriate legal/data agreements and revalidate thresholds
Retire free-tier keep-alive behavior under an owner-approved paid reliability envelope

resumeBulletCandidates.bullet: Built a deployed Graph RAG investigation workspace with Flask, pgvector, Neo4j, ONNX embeddings, cited evidence, and calibrated refusal, achieving 0.887 strict entity F1 on a 455-document synthetic corpus.
Evaluated vector and graph-expanded retrieval by query category, improving relationship-query hit@5 from 0.500 to 0.833 while documenting dense-corpus tradeoffs.

projects.title: Legal Document Intelligence RAG
projects.summary: A deployed Azure RAG research workspace for citation-grounded questions over public M&A litigation and transaction documents.
projects.outcome: A versioned public-document pipeline turns court opinions and SEC filings into 3,055 searchable chunks and returns evidence-linked answers with an explicit refusal path.

deployment.runtime: Flask and Gunicorn on Azure App Service with managed identity, Azure AI Search, and Blob Storage

disclosure.source: Official public Delaware court opinions and public SEC transaction documents registered with source URLs and checksums
disclosure.license: Public official-source documents; source-specific terms and United States government/public-record status apply
disclosure.permittedUse: Read-only portfolio demonstration, retrieval evaluation, and engineering research with source attribution
includedFields: Public document text and extracted structural elements
Case, court, filing, section, page, checksum, and canonical source metadata
Embeddings and retrieval chunks derived from the registered public corpus
excludedFields: Client, firm, user-uploaded, confidential, privileged, and personal matter data
Private credentials, local environment files, and raw authorization material
Legal opinions, attorney work product, and production discovery decisions
deployedArtifactContents: A promoted Azure AI Search index containing 3,055 chunks derived from approved public documents
Public-source citation metadata and aggregate evaluation results
Read-only Flask application code; no private user-upload workflow

evidence.claim: The 45-question release benchmark recorded retrieval hit rate@8 1.0 and citation-provenance validity 1.0.
evidence.method: Run the versioned gold-qa-v2-delaware-expansion evaluation against the configured promoted retrieval index.
evidence.scope: 45-question gold-qa-v2-delaware-expansion benchmark over the promoted 3,055-chunk public index
evidence.environment: Azure AI Search promoted r3 index
evidence.caveat: The benchmark measures retrieval hit rate and citation provenance, not legal-answer correctness.

evidence.claim: The current Azure App Service application root returned HTTP 200.
evidence.method: Read-only HTTP request with redirects followed; no user data submitted.
evidence.scope: Azure App Service application root only
evidence.caveat: HTTP reachability is not availability, confidentiality, security, or production-readiness evidence.

evidence.claim: The deployed retrieval corpus is derived from registered public court and SEC sources, not confidential client documents.
evidence.method: Review the versioned source registry, checksums, production index inventory, and documented environment boundary.

evidence.claim: The repository test suite passed locally when source import resolution was made explicit.
evidence.method: Run `PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` after detecting stale editable-install paths in the generated virtual environment.
evidence.scope: Repository unit and integration test suite
evidence.caveat: Passing repository tests does not establish production availability or legal-answer accuracy.

narrative.recruiterSummary: Legal teams need answers that stay attached to the source, especially when documents are long and high stakes. This project demonstrates an evidence-first research workflow over public M&A litigation and transaction documents: a reviewer asks a question, receives a grounded answer, and can inspect the cited document, section, and page rather than trusting an unsupported response.
narrative.technicalNarrative: Versioned adapters ingest public PDFs through Azure Document Intelligence and public SEC HTML through a native parser, normalize them into stable records, and build structure-aware chunks. Azure AI Search retrieves the promoted public corpus; Azure OpenAI generates only from that evidence, while the Flask workspace exposes research, corpus, evaluation, and health views. Managed identity separates deployed resources from local credentials, and the corpus index is promoted independently from application deployment.
limitations: The public endpoint is anonymous and does not have the controls required for confidential legal matters.
The evaluation does not establish legal-answer correctness or legal advice quality.
Some source-specific reuse terms may differ even though the documents are available from official public sources.
HTTP reachability does not establish an availability, confidentiality, security, or production SLO.
scalabilityRoadmap: Add attorney-reviewed answer and citation-correctness evaluation beyond retrieval and provenance checks
Replace the residual style-based legal-outline parser heuristics with a branch-aware outline state machine
Add authenticated matter isolation, encrypted private storage, malware scanning, retention, and audit controls before any user uploads
Move ingestion and index construction to durable background workflows with reviewed index promotion
Add quota, cost, abuse, availability, and security monitoring appropriate to an owner-approved production service

resumeBulletCandidates.bullet: Built and deployed an Azure RAG workspace using Document Intelligence, AI Search, Azure OpenAI, managed identity, and citation-required generation over a 3,055-chunk public legal corpus.

Versioned and evaluated a 45-question legal retrieval benchmark, recording 1.0 retrieval hit rate@8 and 1.0 citation-provenance validity while explicitly separating those metrics from legal-answer accuracy.

projects.title: Text-to-SQL Interface with Guardrails and Hallucination Detection
projects.summary: An approval-gated analyst console that turns bounded natural-language questions into policy-checked, read-only SQL over disclosed synthetic data.
projects.outcome: Reviewers can inspect SQL, assumptions, schema lineage, policy checks, and a bounded result preview before one single-use execution; unsafe, malformed, identifier-exposing, and hallucinated-schema queries fail closed.

deployment.runtime: Scale-to-zero FastAPI container using the committed demo fixture and ephemeral SQLite proposal state

disclosure.source: Hand-authored synthetic demo fixture inspired by the MoMTSim V2 synthetic mobile-money dataset (DOI 10.17632/zhj366m53p.2)
disclosure.license: MoMTSim V2 is CC BY 4.0; the deployed rows are repository-authored synthetic fixtures rather than redistributed source rows
disclosure.permittedUse: Portfolio demonstration, deterministic evaluation, and bounded analyst-workflow review
includedFields: Synthetic payment date, amount, status, channel, country, and segment
Synthetic payment and customer keys used only as internal fixture join mechanics
excludedFields: Source initiator and recipient account identifiers
Real customer, cardholder, bank, credential, and personal data
Identifier-like fields in model context and public result previews
The locally generated 4,225,958-row approved DuckDB snapshot
deployedArtifactContents: No raw source CSV and no data/approved snapshot artifact

evidence.claim: All 18 deterministic policy cases matched their expected trusted or refused outcomes.
evidence.method: uv run python scripts/run_evaluation.py against the committed synthetic fixture
evidence.scope: 18 trusted and refused cases over the committed synthetic fixture
evidence.caveat: The fixture and case set are intentionally bounded and do not establish open-ended semantic correctness.

evidence.claim: Six status-only public route, fixture-boundary, and deployed-control checks passed for the anonymous live demo.
evidence.method: HTTP checks with response bodies limited to status and disclosed fixture metadata
evidence.scope: Root, evaluation, examples, safe preview, active fixture boundary, and deployed control configuration
evidence.environment: Azure Container Apps anonymous live demo
evidence.caveat: Status-only checks do not establish availability, caller authorization, durable limits, or production readiness.

evidence.claim: The active public revision reports the committed demo fixture, not the local approved snapshot.
evidence.method: Verified /v1/status snapshot state and fixture SHA-256

evidence.claim: The container build context excludes raw source files and data/approved artifacts while retaining only the disclosed fixture and aggregate evidence.
evidence.method: Build the image and run the boundary verifier inside that image

evidence.claim: The deployed dataset is hand-authored synthetic data and source account identifiers are excluded from the approved snapshot contract.
evidence.method: Versioned provenance, license, source checksums, and curated-field classification

evidence.claim: An owner-authenticated local lifecycle generated, approved once, revalidated, and executed a bounded aggregate proposal.
evidence.method: Status-level local integration verification using Microsoft Entra ID; no token, question, SQL, or rows retained
evidence.result: verified locally; not a public SLO

evidence.claim: The anonymous non-production target has a redacted owner notification route, bounded budget thresholds, and aggregate stderr and latency alerts.
evidence.method: Read-only Azure configuration observation with recipient and log data excluded
evidence.result: one enabled action group, $30 monthly budget, and two enabled five-minute scheduled-query alerts
evidence.scope: Existing zero-to-one-replica Azure Container App demo
evidence.caveat: Budgets do not prevent spend; alerts and process-local telemetry do not establish availability, SLO, or production readiness.

narrative.recruiterSummary: Natural-language analytics is attractive because it lowers the barrier to data access, but executing model-generated SQL directly creates obvious security, privacy, and correctness risk. This project turns that risky shortcut into a reviewable workflow: the model may propose, a deterministic policy engine must validate, and a person must approve one bounded read-only preview.
narrative.technicalNarrative: FastAPI separates proposal from execution. Azure OpenAI receives only an identifier-excluding semantic catalog through Microsoft Entra authentication; SQLGlot checks statement shape, functions, tables, columns, identifier projection, and ranking semantics; DuckDB EXPLAIN and resource limits run before a short-lived approval can be consumed. Execution revalidates both SQL policy and the active snapshot checksum.
limitations: The current endpoint is anonymous and has no caller authorization.
The deployed rate and proposal-budget controls are process-local and reset after scale-to-zero or restart.
Approval state is ephemeral and single-replica.
The model can still propose semantically wrong SQL, so human review remains mandatory.
The anonymous demo has no automatic expiry; the owner remains responsible for ongoing cost and operational review.
scalabilityRoadmap: Replace ephemeral SQLite with an owner-approved transactional store and prove cross-replica single-use consumption
Enable single-tenant Microsoft Entra authentication and verify unauthenticated denial
Replace process-local rate and proposal budgets with durable distributed controls before multi-replica hosting
Add alerting, budget ownership, availability/error monitoring, and an owner-approved load envelope
Expand semantic evaluation with reviewer-approved equivalent SQL rather than literal query matching

resumeBulletCandidates.bullet: Built an approval-gated Text-to-SQL service with Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Entra ID, SQLGlot, FastAPI, and read-only DuckDB execution, matching expected outcomes across 18 deterministic safety and correctness cases.

Designed a checksum-pinned synthetic-data release boundary that removes source account identifiers, blocks raw and approved snapshots from the container image, and exposes only classified fields to model context and previews.

Delivered and verified a scale-to-zero Azure Container Apps demo with immutable revision, image-digest, fixture-boundary, and deployed-control evidence while explicitly separating anonymous exposure from production readiness.
